subject: ACCT
title: Introductory Financial Accounting
description: Introduction to accounting for business organizations. Reporting of financial results of operations and financial position to investors, managers, and others. Emphasis on the use of accounting information for decision making.

subject: ACCT
title: Accounting Principles
description: Introduction to basic accounting principles and practices. Emphasis is placed on the accounting cycle and the key financial statements necessary for business decisions. Introduces basic financial and managerial accounting concepts.

subject: ACCT
title: Introductory Managerial Accounting
description: An introduction to the use of accounting within an organizational context. Emphasis is placed on the development and dissemination of accounting information necessary for effective management including: planning, directing, motivating, and controlling activities and behaviours.

subject: ACCT
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
description: Financial accounting from a producer point of view. Topics include cash, receivables, inventories, short and long-term investments, intangible assets and capital assets including the appropriate financial statement considerations.

subject: ACCT
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
description: Financial accounting from a producer point of view. Topics include accounting for liabilities, shareholders equity, leases, future income taxes, pensions, accounting changes and earnings per share including the relevant financial statement considerations.

subject: ACCT
title: ESG and Sustainability Reporting
description: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance is the key to unlocking the power of business today - to build a better tomorrow. Expand your professional opportunities by learning how to measure, analyze, and report on ESG.

subject: ACCT
title: Accounting for SMEs
description: Covers accounting from the perspective of small or medium-sized enterprise (SME) or a new business venture - and investigates the interplay between accounting and informed, strategic decision-making.

subject: ACCT
title: Contemporary Topics in Accounting
description: Examination of selected contemporary topics in accounting.

subject: ACCT
title: Cost Accounting
description: The production of accounting data for the purpose of decision-making, control and evaluation. Topics covered are in the cost classifications and methods of cost establishment, cost data appropriate for decision models, standards and controls.

subject: ACCT
title: Taxation
description: Taxation levied on profits, sales, property and estates and its impact upon management decisions. Consideration will be given to the biases and shifts implicit in any system of taxation.

subject: ACCT
title: Advanced Taxation

subject: ACCT
title: Auditing

subject: ACCT
title: Advanced Financial Accounting

subject: ACCT
title: Accounting Theory

subject: ACCT
title: Managerial Control Systems
description: Case approach to Management Control Systems explaining the use of accounting data from a managerial perspective. Emphasis is placed on how managers use planning and control to accomplish a firm's strategies.

subject: ACCT

subject: ACCT
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
description: Provides detailed coverage of the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) primarily related to assets. Emphasizes the theory behind the methods, the strengths and weaknesses of such methods and the need for sound professional judgement.

subject: ACCT
title: Financial Statement Analysis
description: Covers the theories, concepts and practices of financial statement analysis with an emphasis placed on applications.

subject: ACCT
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
description: Builds on Intermediate Financial Accounting I with coverage of the Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) primarily related to liabilities and owners' equity. Emphasizes the theory behind the methods, the strengths and weaknesses of methods and the need for sound professional judgment.

subject: ACCT
title: Advanced Financial Accounting
description: Focuses on advanced accounting methods related to inter-corporate investments and financial reporting. subject: ACCT
title: Accounting Theory
description: Examines the conceptual framework underlying the preparation of financial accounting information, and the theories and propositions on the use of such information by investors, regulators, standard setters, and other corporate stakeholders.

subject: ACCT
title: Integrative Accounting I
description: Integrated application of the technical CPA competencies relating to financial reporting, audit, finance, taxation, and performance management within case scenarios that provide a rich professional context.

subject: ACCT

description: Further development of taxation competency by focusing on tax compliance and planning issues for individuals, corporations, trusts and partnerships within case scenarios, which focus on tax implications of business decisions.

subject: ACCT

description: Provides intermediate level discussions to the production and analysis of costs used for pricing, production and investment decisions, revenue analysis, performance evaluation, management incentive systems and strategy analysis.

subject: ACCT
title: Managerial Control Systems

subject: ACCT
title: Auditing

subject: ACCT
title: Advanced Auditing
description: Further development of assurance competencies necessary to perform internal audit projects and external assurance engagements, including assessing needs, developing and performing procedures, and documenting and reporting results for realistic case scenarios.

subject: ACCT
title: Integrative Accounting II
description: Integrated application of the CPA competencies of strategy, governance in management accounting within case scenarios that demonstrate how to build control systems and perform financial analysis for different entities.

subject: ALMC

subject: ALMC

subject: ALMC

subject: ALMC

description: Increases reading, writing, listening, and speaking skills in Modern Standard Arabic through the study of a given topic. Topics may include Arabic news media, literature, and historical texts. A continuation of Arabic Language and Muslim Cultures 331.

subject: ALMC

subject: ALMC
title: Topics in Colloquial Spoken Arabic II

subject: DSGN

subject: DSGN
title: Capstone Studio in Architecture
description: Capstone studio in the Bachelor of Design in City Innovation Architecture Concentration. Projects engage contemporary issues defining the built and natural environments.

subject: DSGN
title: Work Integrated Learning Studio in Landscape Architecture
description: Work Integrated Learning (WIL) studio in the Bachelor of Design in City Innovation Landscape Architecture Concentration. Students connect with community partners to address compelling local issues in the built urban environment.

subject: DSGN
title: Capstone Studio in Landscape Architecture
description: Capstone studio in the Bachelor of Design in City Innovation Landscape Architecture Concentration. Projects engage contemporary issues defining the built and natural environments.

subject: EALS

description: A research-oriented seminar to synthesize students' training in East Asian languages and cultures and bring it to bear on a particular subject in Chinese and/or Japanese, or on the relation between East Asian languages and their respective cultures.

prerequisites_raw: Consent of the Department.
description: Exploration of the interactions between humans and environment at different time scales and in different regions. Geographically distinct regions are selected to highlight how humans have adapted to climate change and hazardous natural events. Past adaptations will be examined in the modern context.

subject: EASC
title: Topics in Methods in Earth Science
prerequisites_raw: Consent of the Department.
description: An introduction to field and laboratory methods used in earth surface processes research. Field excursions may involve travel and will provide the basis for laboratory exercises.

subject: EASC
title: Research Project: Topics in Earth Science
description: An original research project that focuses on earth surface processes and may target local, regional, or global issues. subject: EAST

prerequisites_raw: East Asian Studies 201 and completion of 60 units
description: An investigation of East Asian countries and their relations with non-East Asian countries and global initiatives. The focus will be on either China, Japan or Korea and may include culture, politics, business, environment, etc.

description: Contemporary social, philosophical, economic, political and/or international issues within East Asia and methodologies for analysis of the basis for interactions among East Asian countries will be presented in-depth.

prerequisites_raw: Biology 313; and Biology 315 or Environmental Science 401.

subject: ECOL

subject: ECOL

description: A conceptual and practical treatment of population ecology including: population growth, demography, life histories, population dynamics, competition, predation and mutualism.

subject: ECOL

description: A class project course in which students apply their understanding of ecological and evolutionary concepts and their analytical skills to investigate selected problems in detail. subject: ECOL

description: The ecology of fishes with an emphasis on freshwater systems. Topics covered include: morphology, systematics, foraging

subject: ECOL
title: Research Project in Ecology
description: Research project under the co/supervision of faculty members in the Department of Biological Sciences. Original and independent thought, practical research, and written and oral reports presented on completion of this course.

subject: ECOL

subject: ECOL

description: Research project under the co/supervision of faculty members in the Department of Biological Sciences. description: Directed training in field/laboratory methods and research.

subject: ECOL
title: Directed Research in Ecology II
description: Directed training in field/laboratory methods and research.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Principles of choice under scarcity and the role of institutions, especially markets, for the production and distribution of goods and services: what and how much gets produced, how is it produced, and who gets what is produced.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: Measurement of economic activity, economic growth, money and financial systems, international economy and exchange rates, business cycles, unemployment and inflation, and macroeconomic policies.

subject: ECON
title: (ENGG 209) Engineering Economics
description: The basic tools and methodology of engineering economic studies. Topics include investment decisions, theory of replacement, economies of scale, externalities, social decision making and government regulation. Examples are drawn from engineering projects.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Coding and Data
description: Introduction to the logic and practice of coding and the core elements of statistical analysis of data as they apply in economics and the social sciences more broadly.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Economic Theory - Microeconomics I
description: Economic methodology, consumer theory, theory of the firm, competitive markets, efficiency, and the role of economics in public policy.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Economic Theory - Macroeconomics I
description: Theories of long-run economic performance and Keynesian economic models for the analysis of short-run economic fluctuations, the role of expectations, and stabilization policies.

subject: ECON

description: Use of spreadsheets for economics applications, including project evaluation with financial-economic functions, oil and gas prospect evaluation, investment portfolio management with database functions, database retrieval, and various topics in micro and macroeconomics.

subject: ECON
title: The Global Trading System

subject: ECON

subject: ECON
title: Development Economics

subject: ECON

description: The growth and development of the Canadian economy in relation to the endowment of natural resources, changing market conditions and technology, and Canadian public policy.

subject: ECON
title: Money and Banking

subject: ECON

subject: ECON

subject: ECON

subject: EDUC

subject: EDUC

subject: EDUC

subject: EDUC

description: A clinical seminar in elements of family law practice. The clinical experience may be obtained through simulated exercises, supervised handling of files and/or placements. Topics include Chambers advocacy, marital dispute consultations and drafting of a settlement.

subject: LAW

description: A clinical seminar involving placements in any one of the following practice areas: energy law, resources law, water law, and environmental law.

description: The provisions of the Income Tax Act applicable to corporations and their shareholders. Topics include the classification of corporations for tax purposes, the taxation of corporate income, the taxation of corporate distributions, and the taxation of various types of corporate reorganizations.

description: Basic principles, policies, and procedures governing immigration and refugee law. subject: LAW
title: Graduate Seminar in Legal Research and Methodology
description: Preparation for developing, researching and writing a thesis or major research paper. The distinctive nature of legal scholarship and its professional context will be explored. Students will be introduced to specific research techniques and to the challenges of comparative and cross-cultural work.

subject: LAW
title: Graduate Seminar in Legal Theory
description: An exploration of schools of legal theory, with the goal of helping students situate their graduate research within one or more of those approaches to legal scholarship. title: Major Research Paper I
description: Reflects extensive research on a topic in law and proposes a solution to a problem or presents a critical evaluation of an issue in this area of law. subject: LAW
title: Major Research Paper II
description: Building on Law 707 and in consultation with their supervisors, students complete an original research paper.

subject: LAW
title: Special Topics in Law

Directed readings course aimed at preparing doctoral students for writing their proposals or for acquiring legal knowledge in their area of research.

subject: LEAD
title: Foundations in Ethical Leadership
description: Evidence-based approach to leadership with an emphasis on self-awareness and personal development. Students will learn the behaviours that predict leader emergence and leadership effectiveness.

subject: LEAD
title: Leadership Studies Capstone
description: Students advance their practical understanding of effective leadership behaviours, and build capacity to facilitate leadership skills in others.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Linguistics I
description: Introduction to the scientific study of language, including the analysis of word, sentence, and sound structure, and the exploration of language as a human, biological, social, and historical phenomenon.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Linguistics II
description: Further introduction to the scientific study of language. Topics include: language change, language acquisition, language families and areas, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics, bilingualism, and writing systems.

subject: LING
title: Modern English Grammar
description:
A comprehensive exploration of contemporary English. The course is based on modern linguistic analysis, but also includes traditional grammatical terminology, as well as language change, attitudes to language varieties and problems in usage.

Also known as:  (formerly Linguistics 321)

subject: LING
title: Language and Advertising
description: An investigation of the nature of persuasive messages from the perspective of linguistic theory. Topics may include truth and falsity, implication, ambiguity, and context-dependence.

subject: LING
title: Varieties of English
description: Survey and analysis of the varieties of English currently spoken in the world, including various dialects, especially Canadian and American, and English-based pidgins and creoles.

subject: LING
title: Rap Linguistics
description: The leading music genre known as rap is dominated by language. Explores how this creatively flourishing art-form relates to language science. An examination of the manipulation of sounds, words, grammar, and meaning in rap, and what it reveals about language in the mind and in society.

subject: LING
title: Syntax I
description: Introduction to syntax. Emphasis on tree-drawing and basic argumentation skills. Topics may include: syntactic categories; grammatical, thematic, and structural relations; syntactic movement.

subject: LING
title: Language in Humans & Machines
description: Overview of key properties of the learning and use of language in humans and machines, discussing both overlap and divergence, as well as the implications for machines as language partners for humans. No previous background in Linguistics or Computer Science is required.

subject: LING
title: Phonology I
description: Theory and practice of phonological analysis: the classical phoneme; distinctive features and their organization; methods of analysis; underlying and surface representations; rules and derivations.

subject: LING
title: Language And Power
description: The nature of the linguistic resources used to create, enhance and justify positions of dominance or subordination, or to influence and persuade populations. Examples drawn from the discourse of gender and ethnic relations, government and business.

subject: LING
title: Language Acquisition I
description: Introduction to basic ideas and issues in first- and second-language acquisition. Adopts a linguistic approach, viewing language acquisition as the acquisition of a "mental grammar", looking at examples from sound, sentence structure, word learning and meaning. Focus on defining the essential proper

subject: LING
title: Introduction To Semantics
description: Introduction to the study of conventional meaning Topics may include: word meaning,, propositional and predicate logic, properties of quantifiers, definite and indefinite descriptions, and pragmatics.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Speech-Language Pathology
description: A comprehensive overview of the subject including: basic components of speech and language, normal language development, communication disorders, and current professional issues.

subject: LING
title: Phonetics I
description: Intensive practice in the perception, production and transcription of speech sounds accompanied by an introduction to the physiology and acoustics of speech.

subject: LING
title: Language and Mind
description:
An overview of central issues in the study of language and its relationship to the human mind. Topics may include the
nature/nurture debate, human specialization for language, and theories of mental representation. 
Prequisite: Linguistics 201.

subject: LING
title: Historical Linguistics I
description: Central topics in the study of language change including: principles and methods of linguistic reconstruction; universals, typologies, and the explanation of language change; sources of language change with a consideration of acquisitional and sociolinguistic factors.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Sociolinguistics
description: Social differentiation of language in terms of the gender, socio-economic status and geographical distribution of speakers.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Pragmatics
description: An introduction to the study of context-dependent meaning. Topics may include: deixis, reference, implicature, presupposition, speech acts, and information structure.

subject: LING
title: (ENGL 381) The History of English
description: An introduction to important changes and stages in the history of English including its Indo-European and Germanic origins and a consideration of Modern English grammar and orthography from a historical perspective.

subject: LING
title: Syntax II
description: A theoretically grounded approach to syntax using data from a variety of languages. Constructing and evaluating syntactic hypotheses. May involve collecting data from a native speaker of a foreign language.

subject: LING
title: Phonology II
description: Recent issues in phonological theory.

subject: LING
title: Morphology I
description: An introduction to the study of word-structure. Inflectional and word-formation morphology, morphological processes, morphological organization, interfaces with phonology and syntax. Practical problems in word analysis.

subject: LING
title: Language Acquisition II
description: In-depth investigation of issues in language acquisition. Topics include differentiating populations of learners (monolingual, bilingual and delayed first-language learners, child and adult second-language learners, heritage language learners) and the exploration of different kinds of research tasks

subject: LING
title: Advanced Semantics
description: Continuing study of conventional meaning accompanied by an introduction to some technical tools used in the field of semantics. Topics may include: compositionality, sets and functions, tense, aspect, modality, and event semantics.

subject: LING
title: Phonetics II
description: Continuing study of the anatomy, physiology and acoustics of speech and related issues in speech research, paralleled by laboratory work in the acoustic and physiological analysis of speech.

subject: LING
title: History of Linguistic Thought
description: A survey of major schools of linguistic thought. Focus on the origin and development of concepts central to contemporary linguistic theory.

subject: LING
title: Historical Linguistics II
description: Theoretical approaches to current topics in the field of historical linguistics. Research methods and practical skills in data collection and analysis.

subject: LING
title: Typology
description: Study of the unity and diversity of the world's languages. How do the grammars of individual languages differ from each other, and in what ways are they all alike? Which characteristics are common across languages, and which are rare? An overview of the methodology and main results of typological re

subject: LING
title: (PSYC 467) Psycholinguistics
description: Exploration of the cognitive, neuropsychological, and social processes that underlie language abilities, with reference to linguistic theory.

subject: LING
title: Topics in Laboratory Linguistics
description: Experiential learning course in which students will develop skills necessary for the collection and analysis of linguistic data. Areas of focus may include (among others) phonetics, syntax, computational linguistics, phonology, and language development.

subject: LING
title: Field Methods for Indigenous Languages
description: Principles and techniques of collecting, editing and analysing elicited linguistic data and associated problems. Practical experience with language consultant(s).

subject: LING
title: Morphology II
description: A survey of issues in morphological theory.

subject: LING
title: Advanced Syntactic Analysis
description: A survey of current work in syntactic theory.

subject: LING
title: Advanced Phonological Analysis
description: An advanced course on current work in phonological theory.

subject: LING
title: Topics in Language Acquisition
description: Exploration of a selected topic related to current research in language acquisition. subject: LING
title: (PHIL519)Formal Semantics of Natural Language
description: Central issues in the logical semantics of natural language, focusing on topics such as quantification, scope, and the interpretation of pronouns.

subject: LING
title: Survey of Indigenous Languages of the Americas
description: A survey of the indigenous languages of the Americas, including classifications of language families and structural analysis of selected languages.

subject: LING

description: Exploration of a selected topic related to current research in phonetics. Topics may include theories of speech perception, speech production, the relationship between phonetics and phonology, sources of phonetic variation, or experimental methodologies used in phonetics research.

title: Topics in Linguistic Analysis

subject: LING
title: Topics in Historical Linguistics
description: An advanced course in the theory of historical linguistics.

subject: LING
title: Statistics for Linguistic Research
description: Introduction to basic statistical concepts, methods of analysis, and quantitative modelling techniques, with a focus on their application to the unique properties of language research and linguistic data.

description: An overview of theory and research methods with a focus on empirical research in the field of applied linguistics. Students will read and critique recent studies, develop research questions, and explore ways in which to answer their questions.

description: Examines theories and approaches in literary, cultural and film criticism. Students will develop research questions and explore ways in which to answer these questions as they relate to cultural artefacts (literary and filmic) in languages other than English.

title: Introduction To Legal Studies
description: Overview of the role of law in society. Examination of different concepts of law. Study of legal rules, institutions, processes and personnel in social context. Discussion of construction and exercise of the power of law. Emphasis on Canadian law and legal system.

description: Examination of the philosophy and science of law as tools of social engineering. Topics may include employment law, civil law, criminal law, reproductive rights and family law. All material is studied as it pertains to the Canadian legal culture.

subject: LWSO

subject: LWSO

description: An examination of the fundamental conceptions of rights and freedoms in the works of J.S. Mill and twentieth- and twenty-first-century philosophers. The treatment of these concepts in contemporary law and their role in contemporary legal and social issues are explored as well.

subject: LWSO
title: Socio-legal Issues in Contemporary Liberal Societies

subject: LWSO

subject: LWSO

description: Students will conduct an independent research project under the direction of a supervisor. In the seminar, students will discuss and present their projects and other topics relevant to conducting research.

subject: LWSO

subject: ZOOL
title: An Introduction to Invertebrate Zoology
description: Natural history and diversity of invertebrates, which include sponges, corals, jellyfish, snails, octopus, insects, crustaceans, sea stars, and various worms. Emphasis on how free-living and parasitic organisms feed, move, reproduce, and survive in marine, freshwater, and terrestrial habitats.

subject: ZOOL
title: An Introduction to Vertebrate Zoology
description: Systematics, natural history and biology of vertebrates, including fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. Laboratory work will emphasize the identification and morphology of native taxa as well as basic techniques of biological systematics.

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Physiology I
prerequisites_raw: Biology 331.
description: Study of control mechanisms in nerves, sensory organs, muscles and endocrine glands.

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Physiology II
prerequisites_raw: Zoology 461.
description: Study of body fluids and hemostasis, body defence systems, reproductive physiology, renal physiology, respiration, circulation, excretion, gastrointestinal physiology and thermoregulation.

subject: ZOOL
title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy
description: The structural, functional, developmental and evolutionary relationships of the organs and systems of the vertebrates. Laboratory work will emphasize the dissection, identification and homologies of structures in various vertebrates.

subject: ZOOL

subject: ZOOL
title: Entomology
description: Introduction to the insects, with emphasis on diversity, evolution, structure/function relationships, behaviour, and ecology.

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Behaviour
description: Offered from an evolutionary and ecological perspective. Development of ethological ideas; interaction of genotype and environment in ontogeny of behaviour; role of behaviour in dealing with environmental challenges.

subject: ZOOL
title: Palaeobiology of Vertebrates
description: Evolutionary trends in the major groups of vertebrates from both neontological and palaeontological viewpoints. The interpretation of palaeontological data and their applicability to our understanding of evolution, systematics and palaeoecology.

subject: ZOOL
title: The Invertebrates
description: Collaborative research experience in invertebrate zoology, with emphasis on discovering, describing, and classifying diversity using zoological collections, systematic theory, and phylogenetic methods.

subject: ZOOL
title: Mammalogy
description: A detailed examination of the evolution, morphology, physiology, ecology and behaviour of mammals.

subject: ZOOL
title: Principles in Parasitism
description: How parasites have evolved, their diverse life strategies, their impact on the natural world, study of most parasitic groups (protozoan, helminth and arthropod parasites) and their characteristics, with a focus on the Canadian context.

subject: ZOOL
title: Evolutionary Perspectives in Neurobiology
description: Explores form, function and performance of invertebrate and vertebrate neurons and nervous systems through examination of physical, biochemical, metabolic, (neuro)physiological and behavioral constraints and trade-offs.

subject: ZOOL

subject: ZOOL
